guest_name: Pilot A — Prior Professional Guest (comedian / Unlicensed Therapy alumna)
why_guest: Appeared on Unlicensed Therapy; existing relationship makes the first-pilot ask low-risk; established comedy voice that plays well against Producer's register
why_now: Re-engagement after prior episode creates natural continuity and a soft test of host chemistry between Host + Producer together
episode_thesis: A comedian who has already opened up on one mic can go further on a two-host format — the second conversation is always more honest than the first
proposed_artifact: Clip package: one two-minute moment of genuine disagreement between all three people that works without setup
contact_route: producer email to prior booking address
next_action: Pull prior episode notes; draft warm re-engagement email via producer
notes: Pilot 1 — proves host chemistry in a low-social-cost environment; contact route already established

guest_name: Pilot B — Producer's World (artist / writer / technologist weak tie)
why_guest: Sits at the intersection of creative practice and systems thinking; Producer has a direct professional relationship that does not require Host's social capital
why_now: Producer's direct network can be activated without drawing on Host's relationship budget; tests whether the show can source guests independently
episode_thesis: Someone who builds things by hand and also thinks structurally will surface the exact tension the show is designed to explore — between instinct and architecture
proposed_artifact: Written artifact produced in-session: one page of working notes or a diagram the guest draws during the conversation; photographed and included in show notes
next_action: Producer to identify specific candidate and draft outreach; no producer intermediary needed
notes: Pilot 2 — tests whether Producer can run a guest relationship end-to-end without Host; also tests segment timing in a two-host format

guest_name: Pilot C — Weak-Tie Crossover (comedy × tech or comedy × music figure)
why_guest: Bridges two audiences and tests the show's ability to find guests outside the immediate Unlicensed Therapy network; relationship is a second-degree connection via shared scene
why_now: The show needs to prove it can land guests who don't already know Host; a publicist route tests the formal intake process before it matters
episode_thesis: A figure who works fluently in two registers — funny and technically rigorous — can demonstrate that the show's format holds even when the guest's primary identity is not 'podcast guest'
proposed_artifact: A short audio clip extracted from the hidden-microphone setup — no visible mic in frame — demonstrating the room-read audio quality as a standalone proof of concept
next_action: Research publicist representation; draft formal inquiry letter via producer
source_provenance: Comedy × tech/music crossover scene; weak-tie referral from shared network
notes: Pilot 3 — tests the formal publicist intake route and the Austin studio logistics; also tests hidden-audio capture quality as a standalone artifact
